elements.content: Grammar focus: Conditionals of Concession & Hypothesis.

Core Rule: Use Even if + Clause to express that an outcome remains unchanged regardless of a hypothetical condition, or Whether + S + V + or + Clause for alternative conditions.

Even if (Hypothetical) — Even if + Present/Past + Clause: Even if fiscal policy were relaxed , inflation would remain sticky.
Even though (Factual) — Even though + Real Tense + Clause: Even though interest rates rose , housing demand surged.
Whether... or (Alternative) — Whether + S + V + or + S + V: Whether the board agrees or dissents , the merger will proceed.
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Which sentence expresses a hypothetical concessive condition?
options: Even if tariffs were eliminated tomorrow, trade balances would take years to adjust.
Even though tariffs were eliminated, trade balances remained unequal.

elements.content: 2. What is the difference between 'Even if' and 'Even though'?
options: 'Even if' introduces a hypothetical condition; 'Even though' introduces a known fact.
'Even if' is used only in the past tense.
